targetAudience.primary: Architects and security engineers building agent harnesses, memory layers and permission review
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands message roles, tool output, persistence and approval gates.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Low-privilege content can be reconstructed into a stronger prompt position and then mistaken for authorized user intent.

whyNow: A primary study over six coding-agent harnesses reports all 13 tested attack objectives succeeding after tool-origin content was reconstructed with user-effective privilege, including under automatic permission review.

externalHook.description: Context reconstruction preserves instruction text while upgrading its effective authority.

coreProposition: Reconstructed message role is not sufficient authority provenance: original principal, origin channel, privilege class and any trusted privilege transition must remain independently inspectable across persistence, summarization, handoff and context reconstruction.

originalValue.description: Separates conversational role from authority provenance and treats persistence and handoff as privilege-preservation boundaries.

readerTakeaway: Authorize high-impact actions from original principal and explicit privilege-transition evidence, not from the role label emitted by prompt assembly.

supported: All 13 tested objectives succeeded across six harnesses in the reported full-access setting.
In three automatic-review harnesses, transformed context succeeded where the conventional comparison was 0/13.
The study covers persistence through goals, scheduled tasks and skill-like mechanisms.
unsupported: A universal mitigation or optimal provenance representation
Production prevalence or organization-specific blast radius
Security of any proposed signed-envelope or capability design
uncertain: How provenance composes through summarization and synthesis

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument is a general agent-harness authority-provenance problem.

decisionReason: The comparative attack results isolate context privilege transformation from ordinary risk review and support an independently valuable architecture boundary.
